document.title: Audience-to-message map
document.summary: This map turns Conduit’s public Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows claims into situation → capability → named-proof → next-action rows for independent hotels, hotel groups, and short-term rental operators. Figures stay attached to a single attributed story; industry-page copy is not treated as a tested campaign winner, and personalization is limited to evidence on the target account.
document.markdown:
This map is for humans and ABM agents choosing what to say, not a guarantee of conversion. Capabilities come from [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities). Numbers come only from named pages in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence) and are Conduit-attributed, not independently verified. Industry landing pages are positioning, not performance-tested ads.

## Message hierarchy

**What the product pages say they do:** [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) answer guest messages and calls using property information and reservation data, take actions in connected tools (for example creating a task or updating a booking), and pass requests to the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**How the work is split:** [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) is the workspace for messages, calls, and handoffs with booking context beside the thread. [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) send confirmations, check-in and checkout messages, follow-ups, and rule-based add-ons. [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) give guests one branded stay link for details, extras, payments, and in-portal questions. Operations (housekeeping, maintenance, inspections) is labeled coming soon in the product nav. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Audiences Conduit already names:** Short-term rentals, Independent Hotels, and Hotel Groups. Do not invent extra segments. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Copy ladder:** the operator’s current situation → the named product that matches the job → what happens with *their* connected tools (only if research supports the connection) → **one** matching customer result with date and caveat → book a demo. Do not lead with G2 4.7/5 widget copy, “perfect guest experience,” or a blended automation rate.

Voice and tone belong in [Brand voice & language](#knowledge/brand-voice); the promise frame belongs in [Positioning & brand promise](#knowledge/brand-messaging).

## Messages by buying situation

Keep the customer name, printed window, and caveat in the same sentence as any figure. Do not average rows.

| Situation | Problem | Capability → claimed value | Specific proof (attributed) | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Independent hotel covering nights while staff work the desk | After-hours calls, late check-in, in-stay requests | Agents use hotel policies and booking details including after hours; Inbox for takeover; workflows/offers for extras such as room upgrades, spa, dining | The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel (using Conduit since Dec 2024): support $4,000→$600/mo; avg reply 57 min→2 min; owner models ≥$3,400/mo NOI and >$500k asset value at 8% cap—not an appraisal or closed sale | Demo after-hours voice + which PMS they actually run (page examples: Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds—not proof of identical write-back) |
| Hotel group | Shared brand, different policies and reservations per property | One workspace; shared brand standards and knowledge; agents use brand voice plus each property’s information; loyalty, upgrades, spa/dining explanations | No named hotel-group case body in this pack—do not borrow STR percentages | Demo parent/child listings, shared KB, and per-property PMS |
| STR operator adding listings | Volume scales with units; split OTA inboxes; overnight lockouts | Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, email, SMS, and calls in one workspace; per-listing knowledge + live PMS; scheduled stay messages; gap-night and add-on workflows | Haven (since Feb 2024): 90% automation across ~270 properties, up from ~40% with few workflows; support need ~25 people → two per shift; scores held 4.8–4.9. HomeHop: ~40→108 listings without extra guest-support hires; 70% automation; voice 1–7 AM | Demo OTA+PMS inbox, listing KB, overnight voice |

Independent hotels: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels). Hotel groups: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups). STR: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals). Lauderdale: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel). Haven: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026). HomeHop: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop).

Use a second STR story only when the account’s situation matches: Cascadia’s first PM acquisition (60% automation and 4.9 communication score across 100 properties); Bocobay leaving Intercom for one inbox; Cosmica Italy/Dubai without expanding support; Canbnb ~1,500 messages/week with 60% handled by AI. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb)

Segment research stays in [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels) and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals).

## Role-specific emphasis

Do not invent buying attitudes. Emphasize jobs that appear in product pages or named stories. Committee shape is in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

| Role in sources | Lead with | Proof that can sit next to it | Do not stretch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Owner / founder (Lauderdale, Cosmica, Bali, Flex) | Coverage without living in Slack; labor vs growth; NOI or exit math | Lauderdale cap-rate model; Bali ~$22k/mo labor, 75 units, 0 extra FTE | Combining Bali (11 VAs replaced) with Haven (nobody laid off because of AI) |
| Guest services / CX (Haven’s Jonathan; Cascadia’s Ryan; Wynwood’s Mayra) | One inbox, history on handoff, quality while automating | Wynwood resolution 14–15 min → 3 min; Cascadia communication score locked at 4.9 | Treating “you cannot tell the difference” as a universal guest outcome |
| Ops / process owner (Canbnb’s Jo-Anne) | Property/team views, guest/owner/vendor inboxes, workflows | Canbnb’s structured inboxes and ~60% of ~1,500 weekly messages | Selling Operations (coming soon) as live housekeeping-at-scale |

Hotel-group cluster and revenue titles on the group page (multi-property operations, room upgrades, direct booking) are demo topics, not proven role outcomes. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

## Offer and call to action

Public product and industry pages use **Book a demo**, not a self-serve checkout. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Draft CTA (not a live campaign, not a claimed relationship): “See how agents would answer after-hours calls for this property and pass exceptions into one inbox.” Name the product that matches the job—Inbox+Agents for omnichannel takeover, Agents for voice, Portals for pre-arrival/waivers/upsells, Workflows for dated sequences. Confirm package coverage in [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing); a bundle rate is not a standalone Agents or Portals price.

Do not offer Operations as generally available. Do not invent a Portals standalone price in outbound copy.

## Proof and personalization boundaries

**Allowed:** the prospect’s industry label as Conduit names it; PMS or channels confirmed in account research *and* listed as supported; **one** matching story with printed dates. An integration logo is not evidence of a supported action—see [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

**Not allowed:** invented partnerships or pains; averaging Haven 90%, Cascadia 60%, HomeHop 70%, Canbnb 60%, and Flex 70%/90%; presenting Lauderdale’s $500k as appraised or sold value; using Guest Favorite share or G2 stars as Conduit KPIs; implying [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) or Operations produced these results (stories name the platform, not those SKUs).

**Keep contradictions visible:** Haven About 230+ vs ~270 properties and 59% vs 55% Guest Favorite; Flex title 70% vs header 90%; HomeHop June 2025 vs “approximately two years”; Bali founded 2025 vs using Conduit since Dec 2024. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays)

Campaign sentences: [Campaign writing examples & rules](#knowledge/writing-examples).
open_questions: Which named hotel-group story, if any, can sit in group-targeted copy given this pack has no group case body?
Which automation denominator (messages, support volume, guest communication) should outbound use when stories disagree?
When, if ever, should Portals or Operations appear in a proof-led CTA before a story isolates them?
How should staffing claims be phrased when Haven reports no AI layoffs and Bali reports replacing eleven VAs?

evidence_notes.statement: Agents are described as answering messages and calls, using context, acting in connected tools, and escalating to the team.
evidence_notes.quote: Answer messages and calls, retrieve context, and take action in your connected tools. Agents escalate to your team when they’re needed.

evidence_notes.statement: The public catalog lists Operations as coming soon for housekeeping, maintenance, and inspections.
evidence_notes.quote:
Operations
Coming soon
AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance and inspections.

evidence_notes.statement: Independent-hotel page positions after-hours answers using hotel policies and booking details.
evidence_notes.quote: Answer guest calls and messages while your team looks after the people at the desk. Conduit uses your hotel’s policies and booking details, including after hours.

evidence_notes.statement: Hotel-group page claims shared brand standards with per-property policies and reservations.
evidence_notes.quote: Handle guest messages and calls across your hotel group. Share brand standards while giving agents the policies and reservation details for each property.

evidence_notes.statement: STR page claims OTA plus messaging and calls in one workspace.
evidence_notes.quote: Bring Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, email, SMS, and calls into one workspace through your connected accounts.

evidence_notes.statement: Haven write-up reports 90% automation across ~270 properties after starting near 40%.
evidence_notes.quote:
Reached
90 percent automation
across 270 properties, up from 40 percent in a few months

evidence_notes.statement: Lauderdale write-up attributes support cost reduction from $4,000 to $600 per month.
Lauderdale owner models $3,400 monthly NOI into more than $500,000 asset value at an 8% cap rate.
evidence_notes.quote: At an 8% Cap Rate, that $3,400 monthly gain translates into over $500,000 in added asset value.

use_when: Drafting ABM or outbound that must pick one industry message
Pairing a named product with a named customer proof
Choosing Book-a-demo CTAs by buying situation
decisions_supported: Whether to lead with independent-hotel after-hours, hotel-group brand consistency, or STR omnichannel scale
Which single attributed story may sit next to a claim
Which product name to put in the CTA versus which to leave out (Operations, unproven Portals)
do_not_infer: Typical or guaranteed automation rates across customers
Hotel-group outcomes or named group logos as proof
That an integration logo means a specific agent action
Invented partnerships, target pains, or tested ad winners
That Portals or Operations caused the named case results
A standalone Agents or Portals price from a bundle
